reasoning_text:
We need to analyze each option conceptual meaning. They are Persian couplets (two lines each). Focus on underlying concepts.

Option 1: "گر به فسون زنده کرد مرده مسیحا - جز سخن خوب نیست سوی من افسون". Rough translation: "If by charm (spell) the dead Christ is revived - there is no enchantment to me except good speech." Something about magic/spell reviving dead, but only good speech matters. Concept: power of speech/words, perhaps resurrection through words.

Option 2: "مرده بودم به سخن های تو گشتم زنده - خفته بودم صفت حسن (beauty) تو بیدارم کرد". Means: I was dead, but your words revived me; I was asleep, your beautiful attribute awakened me. Concept: revival/life through beloved's words/beauty. Similar to option 1 about being revived by speech.

Option 3: "سخن عشق کند در دل افسرده اثر - مرده در گور اگر زنده به تلقین گردد". Means: The word of love has effect on a depressed heart - the dead in the grave can become alive if taught/instilled. Concept: love's word can resurrect even the dead in grave through suggestion. Again revival via love/words.

Option 4: "ما که نظر بر سخن افکنده ایم - مــــــرده اوییـــــم و بـــــدو زنــــده ایــم". Means: We who have cast our gaze upon speech - I am dead and also alive? Actually "مرده اویم و بدو زنده ایم" maybe: "I am dead, yet alive with him". Could be about being dead and alive simultaneously due to love? Let's parse: "ما که نظر بر سخن افکنده ایم" = "We who have set our attention on speech". Then "مرده اویم و بدو زنده ایم" = "I am dead, and with him I am alive". So concept about being dead but alive through someone else. Still about death/life duality.

All seem about death and revival via speech/words/love. Need to find which deviates conceptually.

Let's examine nuance: Option 1 mentions "فسون" (spell) and "مسیحا" (Christ) maybe referencing religious resurrection. It says "except good speech there is no enchantment". Option 2 is personal: your words revived me. Option 3 mentions "سخن عشق" (word of love) affecting depressed heart, dead can be revived by suggestion. Option 4: "ما که نظر بر سخن افکنده ایم" (we who focus on speech) and "مرده اویم و بدو زنده ایم" (I am dead and alive with him). This is similar. Which one differs? Perhaps option 1 introduces concept of "spell" and "Christ" which is more mystical/religious, while others are about personal emotional revival. Option 1's core concept may be about the power of speech itself, not love. Others emphasize love and beloved's words. Option 1 says "except good speech there is no enchantment to me". Could still be about speech's power. Option 3 also about love's word. Option 2 about beloved's words. Option 4 about speech and being dead/alive with someone.

Maybe the odd one is option 1 because it mentions "Christ" and "spell", which is a different conceptual reference (religious resurrection) compared to the others focusing on personal love/beauty.

Alternatively, maybe option 3 is different because it mentions "dead in the grave can become alive if taught" which is about mental suggestion rather than actual emotional revival; but still similar.

Let's compare: Options 2,3,4 talk about personal emotional state: "I was dead, your words revived me", "Love's word revives depressed heart", "I am dead but alive with him". Option 1 is more abstract: "If a spell revives dead Christ, there is no enchantment for me except good speech". It seems to assert that only good speech matters, not magical spells. It's about the speaker's stance on enchantment. The others are about being revived by love. So option 1 deviates.

Thus answer = 1.

Check if any other could deviate: Option 3 includes "dead in the grave" maybe referencing literal death, but still about love's word. Option 1 includes "Christ" which is unique. So answer 1.
